title: Seven decisions for Dinis
kind: decision brief (programmatic animation, played in the browser)
player: docs/board/brief/decisions-brief.html (self-contained; Play, Slides and Storyboard views)
note: Longer than a Reel (studio.c's 45 to 89 s) by design: one scene per decision, for Dinis, not for posting. Beats keep studio.c's {id, narration, visual, facts} shape.

beats.narration: Seven decisions are waiting for you on the AWS programme's decisions page. This brief walks through each one.
beats.visual: Seven numbered tiles appear in a row, each with its short name.

beats.narration: None of them stops the team. Every agent keeps building on the synthetic twin while you decide.
beats.visual: A banner under the tiles: nothing here stops the team.

beats.narration: Each scene shows the problem, the options and the recommendation. Answer by number in pm.aws.a's session.
beats.visual: The recommended answer line types in at the bottom.

beats.narration: Every agent signs its commits with its own key. A key counts only once it is listed in the Factory's keys file.
beats.visual: Key chips, one per agent, on the left; the Factory's keys.json on the right.

beats.narration: factory.c has eight agents' signed key commits verified and waiting, but its session asks your word for every push.
beats.visual: The chips slide up to a closed gate marked factory.c, waiting for your word.

beats.narration: Option a: one standing word, land every verified agent key commit. Option b: a word per landing, as now.
beats.visual: Option a is shown: the gate opens and the chips flow into keys.json.

beats.narration: Recommended: a. More keys are coming tonight, mine among them.
beats.visual: The a option chip lights as recommended.

beats.narration: Every push to dev is checked for an agent's signature, then deployed to the live site that holds the change role.
beats.visual: A commit flows through the signer check to the live site.

beats.narration: Security found three ways round that check: an Owner override line, commits GitHub marks verified, and a checker that runs from the commit it checks.
beats.visual: Three red paths go round the check; a loop shows the checker inside the commit it checks.

beats.narration: Option a: run the checker from main or a pinned commit, and drop the override line. Option b: leave it for now.
beats.visual: Option a: the checker is pinned to main, the override line is struck out.

beats.narration: Recommended: a. It changes .github, which needs your yes.
beats.visual: The a option chip lights as recommended.

beats.narration: Some team paths sit on the hub's own origin: the decisions page, the API layer and the S3 browser's script.
beats.visual: The hub's origin as a large frame holding the app, your sealed session and the change role.

beats.narration: A page there shares the origin with your signed-in session, so a bad change could reach the change role.
beats.visual: A team page enters the frame; a red dashed line runs from it to the session and on to the change role.

beats.narration: Options: a, security reviews every site change before it deploys; b, move team pages to their own area sites; c, both.
beats.visual: A review shield wraps the page, then the page moves out to its own area site.

beats.narration: Recommended: c. Review now, move as the area sites arrive. dev.2.aws.a's code waits on this.
beats.visual: The c option chip lights as recommended.

beats.narration: Template v2.1 fixes R-001, the critical finding: today the change role can make itself account admin.
beats.visual: The change role with a red arrow to account admin, marked R-001 Critical.

beats.narration: v2.1 swaps that for thirteen named IAM actions, allowed only through CloudFormation. Security reviewed it.
beats.visual: The v2.1 box appears and the arrow to admin is cut.

beats.narration: Option a: approve it when you next sign in. Option b: leave it. No work waits on it.
beats.visual: An Approve button appears under the plan.

beats.narration: If you choose 6a, the same console apply covers this one.
beats.visual: A note links decision 4 to decision 6.

beats.narration: You said yes to nine area sites. factory.c has the requests ready in the Factory, waiting for your merge.
beats.visual: The hub in the centre; nine area sites appear around it as dashed outlines.

beats.narration: Each area gets its own site and its own Try the twin link.
beats.visual: The links to each area draw in.

beats.narration: Option a: merge all nine. Option b: only s3 for now. Recommended: a.
beats.visual: All nine outlines turn solid; the a option chip lights as recommended.

beats.narration: Even after v2.1, a script in the page could make the change role admin through a change set, in about four calls.
beats.visual: A chain draws left to right: script in the page, change role, create change set, execute change set, admin.

beats.narration: And the change role can rewrite the DNS role's trust. That role can repoint the site's name, so it is a second way out.
beats.visual: A second red chain drops from the change role to the DNS role's trust and on to the site's name.

beats.narration: iam.aws.a's v2.4 adds permissions boundaries that keep each role to today's scopes, and makes the DNS role's trust console only.
beats.visual: A boundary ring closes round the change role; both red chains are cut.

beats.narration: security.aws.a cleared v2.4 on paper. Before any apply: iam.aws.a's two checks, then your own apply in the console.
beats.visual: A three-line checklist appears: two checks, your console apply, two DNS plans retired.

beats.narration: Recommended: a, by iam and security. b keeps DNS trust edits on the page, c defers the boundaries, d relies on splitting the change page.
beats.visual: The a option chip lights as recommended; b is marked not recommended.

beats.narration: Three agents on account A have work their sessions will not push.
beats.visual: Three agent boxes on the left, each with a stack of commits; GitHub's work branches on the right.

beats.narration: iam.aws.a and dev.1.aws.a cannot push their work branches. viz.aws.a cannot yet turn its key into a git signing key.
beats.visual: Locks appear on the three paths; viz.aws.a shows an extra step, make a signing key.

beats.narration: Option a: say yes in each session. Option b: let viz.aws.a push unsigned. Option c: leave it.
beats.visual: Option a: the locks open and the commits move across to GitHub.

beats.narration: Recommended: a. A work branch is not dev or main, and every commit stays signed.
beats.visual: The a option chip lights as recommended.

beats.narration: Recommended answers: one a, two a, three c, four a, five a, six a, seven a.
beats.visual: The full answer line, large, in the centre.

beats.narration: Type them, or your own, in pm.aws.a's session. I update the page and tell the agents who asked.
beats.visual: Under it: where to answer.
